summary: Learn the effective strategies for adapting urban water systems to climate change. Enroll in our comprehensive training and lead the way in sustainability.
lede: Climate adaptation for urban water systems helps utility managers, engineers and municipal teams assess how climate hazards threaten water services. Participants map vulnerabilities across water and sanitation infrastructure, prioritize interventions using risk, feasibility and value-for-money logic, and plan phased responses that combine engineered and nature-based solutions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who influence decisions affecting water reliability, service continuity, public health, budgets, and climate resilience.
audience: Urban water utility managers and engineers
Climate change adaptation and resilience officers
Water regulators and public sector investment appraisal
Donor-funded program managers and grant officers
Private sector developers and industrial water users
modules: Climate Risks in Urban Water Systems
Climate-Resilient Water Supply and Demand Management
Flood Risk, Stormwater, and Urban Drainage Adaptation
Climate Adaptation for Wastewater and Sanitation Systems
Resilient Asset Management and Infrastructure Upgrades
Economics and Value for Money in Adaptation Investments
prerequisites: Participants should have basic knowledge of urban water systems and a keen interest in climate adaptation strategies. Prior experience in water management, urban planning, or related fields is recommended.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
